title: Workstation Model Service Runbook
summary: Build and operate a bounded local model service on one workstation without confusing locality with security, privacy, or production readiness.
prerequisites: An inventory of CPU, accelerator, memory, storage, operating system, and power constraints
An approved immutable model artifact with license and provenance review
A local-user, data, network, and retention boundary

sections.title: Bound the local service before loading weights
paragraphs: Name the intended user, workload, data classes, prohibited inputs, network exposure, context and output ceilings, expected concurrency, and whether the service may invoke tools. Local execution removes neither the need for authorization nor the risk of prompts, outputs, caches, logs, model files, or tool effects reaching people and systems that should not receive them.

Inventory the exact device and runtime path: operating-system build, drivers, execution provider, runtime or server version, model revision and digest, quantization or conversion, tokenizer and chat template, gateway or client adapter, and configuration. Record model-card limitations and license conditions. Reject mutable aliases and unexplained converted artifacts.

sections.title: Qualify performance, isolation, and restart behavior
paragraphs: Measure model load time, first-output and completion latency distributions, memory and accelerator use, sustained temperature or throttling, disk growth, concurrency, cancellation, malformed requests, and out-of-memory behavior with the real request contract. Reserve capacity for the operating system and other required work; a model that fits once can still destabilize the device under long context, parallel requests, or swap pressure.

Bind the endpoint only where intended, require caller authorization when more than one trust zone can reach it, keep secrets outside prompts and repositories, minimize retained content, and verify that sleep, reboot, runtime failure, and model reload do not silently change identity or policy. Production claims require a supported owner, monitored service objectives, backups, patching, and tested recovery beyond one developer session.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes device and driver inventory, artifact license and digest, runtime compatibility, endpoint and access boundary, representative evaluation results, load and thermal observations, capacity limits, data-handling controls, reboot test, known-good manifest, owner, and review date. Keep measurements dated because drivers, runtimes, model revisions, and device conditions change.

Verify the identity returned by the service rather than trusting a file name. Stop admission on artifact mismatch, unauthorized exposure, protected-data leakage, repeated out-of-memory or thermal failure, critical evaluation failure, or an unrecoverable restart. Close the listener, preserve minimal evidence, reconcile unfinished requests or tool effects, restore the pinned build, and repeat identity, access, evaluation, and load checks before use.

sections.title: Scope, decision rule, and evidence classes
paragraphs: The original guide scope is generic workstation qualification. This worked example narrows that broader scope to one Windows x64 workstation, a CPU-only service bound to 127.0.0.1, fictional nonsensitive prompts, no tool execution, no public endpoint, no gateway, and no production-readiness claim. The pinned server is llama.cpp build b10964, release v0.4.1, commit b29c606e28a01b1bc8c1351026a0fa6e616bf6c4. Its documented lab configuration is two CPU threads, zero GPU layers, parallelism one, no web UI, and alias p42-qwen3-06b. The model artifact is Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf at revision 23749fefcc72300e3a2ad315e1317431b06b590a. See the pinned server documentation at https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b29c606e28a01b1bc8c1351026a0fa6e616bf6c4/tools/server/README.md and the pinned model revision at https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF/tree/23749fefcc72300e3a2ad315e1317431b06b590a.

Use three evidence labels throughout. ACTUAL means a supplied local test or retained receipt recorded the result. FICTIONAL means a classroom input or comparison value invented for teaching and not measured on the workstation. UNKNOWN means the available evidence does not establish the claim. Local evidence remains on the workstation unless the learner deliberately transfers it through an approved process. None of these commands automatically uploads inventory or receipts.

Completed worked input: use the FICTIONAL prompt, "In one short sentence, explain why a public health endpoint does not prove API authentication." The required contract asks for a nonempty completion with max_tokens 64 and temperature 0. The teaching interpretation is that /health can be public while /v1/models and /v1/chat/completions require authentication. The actual conformance receipt deliberately stores contentLength rather than generated text. It evidences that the completion content was nonempty, but does not retain the generated wording. Do not invent or imply that wording is available in the receipt.

The completed decision is PASS only for the tested local learning contract and HOLD for production deployment. Stop admission on an artifact mismatch, unauthorized listener, authenticated identity mismatch, failed authentication test, failed bounded inference, exposed credential, uncertain process ownership, or an untested recovery property being presented as proven. A successful loopback request does not qualify sustained capacity, thermal behavior, privacy, egress, reboot recovery, server-side cancellation, gateway controls, or production security.

sections.title: One-session preflight, unique paths, and privacy-minimized inventory
paragraphs: Open PowerShell at the cloned repository root and keep the same session through all eight sections. This preflight saves the absolute repository root before any Set-Location call. It creates the reusable parent lab-runs if that parent does not exist, but it refuses to reuse the GUID-named run root. The evidence directory is created exactly once. The workspace path is reserved but must not exist because Setup-ServingLab.ps1 requires a new workspace. No system temporary directory is used.

The qualified environment recorded in the supplied lesson evidence is PowerShell 7.6.6, .NET 10.0.12, and CPython 3.13.9 on Windows x64. PowerShell 7.6 or newer is required. The Python code is intended for Python 3.11 or newer, but versions other than 3.13.9 remain unqualified until the same tests pass and are retained on that version.

The inventory contains only facts needed to interpret the exercise: operating-system version and architecture, CPU name and logical processor count, physical memory, free space on the repository drive, and runtime versions. It intentionally omits the computer name, user name, serial numbers, network addresses, and environment variables. Windows documents the queried inventory classes at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-operatingsystem, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-processor, and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-computersystem. Absolute-path validation is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.path.ispathfullyqualified, and Join-Path is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/join-path.

The pinned runtime archive is llama-b10964-bin-win-cpu-x64.zip, 18427629 bytes, with SHA-256 917f39c076402c421224824607397af20f53625a60defc20e8dd22446bf4c5d7. The pinned model is Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf, 639446688 bytes, with SHA-256 9465e63a22add5354d9bb4b99e90117043c7124007664907259bd16d043bb031. These figures come from the supplied qualification record. Setup must independently verify the local files before use.

sections.title: Reuse the saved paths for setup, live conformance, lifecycle tests, and protected cleanup
paragraphs: Continue in the same PowerShell session. Do not recalculate repoRoot from the changed working directory, and do not allocate another baseline workspace or evidence directory. Every lab path below is derived from the saved absolute repoRoot, runRoot, workspace, and evidence variables.

Setup verifies the pinned runtime and model before creating the workspace. The normal setup does not require a cache. The commented ArtifactCache command is an optional alternative when an approved read-only cache already contains both exact artifacts. Cached files must still pass every byte-count, digest, and extracted-tree check.

The baseline generates one server key and keeps it unchanged through Start, the explicit wrong-key request, the successful same-key identity request, conformance, and ownership-checked Stop. A separately generated bad value is sent only in the failing request. The evidence file records status codes and the verified alias, not either credential. All direct HTTP requests have bounded timeouts.

After the baseline server has stopped, the supplied Test-ServingLifecycle.ps1 is actually invoked with a newly created TestRoot and one fresh key retained across that test's owned start, stop, restart, identity recovery, and final stop. The supplied test, rather than prose alone, exercises preservation of a foreign directory, rejection of a changed-byte runtime archive, refusal to start on an occupied port, refusal to stop forged state, and owned restart. RandomNumberGenerator usage is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.randomnumbergenerator.

sections.title: Completed result, evidence classification, and causal failure diagnosis
paragraphs: ACTUAL sample observation from the supplied qualifying run: at 2026-09-20T08:11:15Z, the service ran on 127.0.0.1:11842. The receipt recorded nine observed checks: health_public; authentication_rejection with HTTP 401; server_identity with alias p42-qwen3-06b; bounded_completion containing 141 characters; stream containing 112 characters and completing in 7.660935 seconds; early_disconnect; recovery_after_disconnect containing 141 characters; client_timeout; and overload_observation with four outcomes of HTTP 200. Total receipt duration was 34.4745 seconds. These are actual sample observations from that run, not predictions or guarantees for the learner's run.

The same 12-check receipt recorded three checks as not-observed: server_side_cancellation, stop_restart_recovery, and artifact_hashes. Setup and lifecycle records can establish artifact verification and owned restart separately, but they must not be rewritten as observations made by the port-only client. The receipt records that request contents and credentials were not retained.

The reproducible diagnosed failure is wrong-key authentication. The baseline sends a separately generated bad credential to the authenticated /v1/models endpoint and requires HTTP 401. It then sends the unchanged server-lifecycle key to the same endpoint and requires HTTP 200 plus alias p42-qwen3-06b. Cause: the bad request credential does not match the key held by the running server. Correction: use the same current-session P42_SERVING_API_KEY for Start, authenticated requests, conformance, and Stop. Do not replace the server key, pass a secret in a command-line argument, or infer authentication success from public /health.

If the learner instead gets a connection failure, identity mismatch, timeout, or occupied-port error, do not label it a wrong-key failure. Connection failure concerns listener availability. Identity mismatch concerns the authenticated service reached. Timeout establishes only that the client deadline expired. Occupied-port refusal means another process already owns the requested address. Diagnose the narrow observed cause and preserve the failed evidence.

Review the new local receipt rather than copying the sample values. The following command checks the 12-entry schema and prints only check classifications. It does not expose prompts, outputs, or credentials.

sections.title: Qualification gates and honest unknowns
paragraphs: Capacity and latency remain UNKNOWN. Establish them by running repeated bounded fictional prompts on the target workstation under an approved plan, retaining request count, concurrency, failures, first-output latency, completion latency, and calculated percentiles. The four-response overload sample and one total duration do not establish a sustained-capacity limit, a queueing policy, or a service-level objective.

Memory and thermal behavior remain UNKNOWN. Establish them by recording process memory, system memory pressure, disk growth, CPU utilization, and approved temperature or throttling telemetry during sustained bounded work. A successful completion does not establish an out-of-memory boundary, thermal safety, clock stability, or power behavior.

Privacy and egress remain UNKNOWN beyond the narrow local evidence. Establish them by reviewing listener ownership, firewall policy, process connections, DNS and network telemetry, endpoint-monitoring behavior, backups, log retention, deletion procedures, and the actual contents of receipts and logs. Loopback binding reduces exposure but does not prove that every workstation component keeps data local.

Sleep, resume, and reboot recovery remain UNKNOWN. Establish them under an approved change window by performing an ownership-checked stop, confirming closure, rebooting or resuming, starting only from the verified workspace, and repeating artifact, listener, authenticated identity, inference, disconnect recovery, and owned-stop checks. Preserve before-and-after timestamps and state records.

Server-side cancellation remains UNKNOWN. A client timeout or disconnect proves only client behavior. Establish cancellation with server-owned telemetry correlated to a specific request and evidence that generation work ended. TLS, gateway rate limiting, multiuser authorization, public exposure controls, and production auditing are outside this loopback lab and remain unqualified.

Recovery is fail closed. Preserve failed evidence, identify the narrow cause, restore the pinned artifact and policy without weakening supplied tests, and create a fresh receipt. Never repair an artifact mismatch by changing an expected digest, repair an occupied port by killing a process by name, or reinterpret a not-observed check as PASS.

sections.title: Transfer questions across model families and providers
paragraphs: Do not copy Qwen identifiers, digests, tokenizer assumptions, chat templates, or llama.cpp flags to another model. For every candidate, ask: What exact artifact and immutable revision are approved? What digest identifies the bytes? What license and use restrictions apply? Which runtime, quantization, tokenizer, chat template, context limit, and hardware path are supported? Does the candidate satisfy the same health, authenticated identity, bounded completion, SSE termination, timeout, disconnect, restart, and recovery contract?

Apply those questions independently to Meta/Llama, Microsoft/Phi, Mistral, DeepSeek, NVIDIA, and Z.ai candidates. This provider breadth is a checklist, not evidence that a particular model exists, is downloadable, is license-compatible, or works with the pinned runtime. No candidate URL, benchmark result, compatibility result, or availability result is supplied here. Each candidate answer is therefore UNKNOWN until an approved first-party model card or repository, immutable artifact record, license review, and fresh local conformance evidence are retained.

Also require direct evidence for memory, latency, sustained concurrency, thermal behavior, cancellation, privacy, egress, sleep, reboot, and rollback. A friendly model alias is not a digest. A successful prompt is not proof of the tokenizer or template contract. A benchmark published for different hardware, precision, context, or software is not a local capacity measurement.

The transfer decision is PASS only for the explicitly tested subset and exact candidate artifact. Otherwise record HOLD, retain the verified Qwen workspace for rollback, and compare failures without editing the supplied conformance client or lifecycle scripts.

sections.title: Independent changed task: move only the service port to 11901
paragraphs: Attempt this task before reading the next section. Continue in the same PowerShell session and reuse the actual baseline workspace created earlier. Change only the serving port from 11842 to 11901. Do not rerun setup into a different workspace.

Use the supplied Start-ServingLab.ps1, conformance.py, Stop-ServingLab.ps1, and Test-ServingLifecycle.ps1 without editing them. Produce a fresh changed-port receipt and separate lifecycle restart evidence. Assert that the receipt records port 11901. Stop the owned service before removing its key.
Keep the standard conformance request unchanged, including max_tokens 64 and temperature 0. Altering the output bound would create a different, unqualified experiment and does not satisfy this task.

Explain which properties must remain invariant: runtime and model pins, alias p42-qwen3-06b, authentication source, context 2048, two CPU threads, zero GPU layers, parallelism one, and the unchanged conformance checks. Explain which properties change: listener port, endpoint URLs, process instance, and fresh evidence paths.

A complete result requires owned state for 11901, listener and process ownership, public health, authentication rejection, authenticated identity, bounded completion, SSE termination, disconnect recovery, timeout classification, overload observation, owned stop, and supplied restart testing. A public health response alone cannot distinguish the intended authenticated service from an unrelated process.

sections.title: Complete port-change answer and causal grading feedback
paragraphs: Complete answer: reuse the saved repoRoot, runRoot, workspace, and evidence variables from the baseline session. First confirm that baseline state is stopped. The optional old-port probe below accepts only SocketError.ConnectionRefused as proof that 11842 is closed. It waits at most five seconds, unwraps a fault with GetBaseException(), and treats a timeout, successful connection, cancellation, or any other socket error as inconclusive or failed evidence. TcpClient and SocketError behavior are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.sockets.tcpclient.connectasync and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.sockets.socketerror.

Create a fresh changed-port evidence directory under the existing run root, but do not replace the existing evidence or workspace. Generate one new key for the 11901 live lifecycle. Start on 11901, run unchanged conformance, assert the receipt port and expected identity, and perform ownership-checked Stop while that same key remains set. Then generate a separate lifecycle-test key, create a new TestRoot, and invoke the supplied lifecycle test on 11901 so restart and all four negative cases are exercised rather than narrated.

Expected result: the listener and URLs move to 127.0.0.1:11901 while the runtime, model, alias, context, thread count, GPU-layer count, parallelism, max_tokens 64, and temperature 0 remain invariant. The new port-only receipt still does not prove artifact hashes or server-side cancellation. Setup and lifecycle evidence remain separate.

Causal grading: full credit requires connecting the changed input to the listener, receipt port, and client destination while preserving artifact and serving identity. Deduct for inventing a baseline workspace, recomputing repoRoot after changing directory, editing conformance.py, changing max_tokens, using different keys for Start and its client, clearing the key before Stop, overwriting baseline evidence, accepting /health as authentication proof, stopping by process name, or treating a response from an unrelated listener as sufficient.

Diagnose failures by cause. ConnectionRefused on 11901 means no listener accepted the connection at that instant. Startup refusal on an occupied port means another process owns the address. HTTP 401 or 403 on an authenticated endpoint means the request credential was missing or did not match the running lifecycle. An alias mismatch means the authenticated service is not the required serving identity. A receipt-port mismatch means the retained evidence does not describe the requested endpoint. A client timeout does not prove server cancellation. Preserve the failed evidence, correct the cause, and use another fresh receipt path.
